blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Technology & SaaS, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Usage telemetry accumulates but never becomes product; data products stall on privacy questions and entitlement plumbing.
Deploy frequency rises while incident load eats roadmap; error budgets exist in slide decks, not in release policy.
Teams bolt on LLM features with no cost telemetry, no eval harness and no guardrails; margins erode silently per customer.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
Product events into governed analytics with feature-level cost attribution (product decisions on real unit economics)
Clean rooms, entitlements and metering for customer-facing insights (second revenue line launched)
Protected via routing, caching and eval gates

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 and GDPR/CCPA. Customer-data processing, DPAs and subprocessor duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
